caption: Sees everything that can happen to the target block on one output: placed, removed, changed, reshaped by its neighbors, or only updated (13 blocks, reacts in 1 tick). It is the fast piston BUD below plus an observer: the observer catches reshaping, which no piston can feel, and kicks the piston, so every event gives the same 5-tick pulse. Detail: a stone on the slime block cuts the step between two dusts; the piston, armed by quasi-connectivity (power that reaches it only through the block above it, so it has not noticed it yet), takes the stone off the step in the tick after a block update; the observer under the low dust watches the target below the piston and its pulse climbs into the low dust, lighting the output and updating the piston.

Turns on at the first block update next to the target and stays on until you reset it: the smallest latched BUD, 2 blocks. A sticky piston is powered without having noticed it (the power reaches it only through the block above its neighbor, called quasi-connectivity); the first update makes it notice and push a redstone block next to the output, where it stays. Detail: the reset input is the arming redstone block itself: taking it away updates the piston, it retracts and pulls the block back (the output goes off 1 tick later); putting it back arms it without an update. A change by shape alone sends no block update: not detected.

A classic BUD (it sees pure block updates, which no observer can) that never jams, even on two updates 2 ticks apart: 5 blocks. Two plain pistons pass a package back and forth: a slime block carrying the arming redstone block and an observer. Detail: piston P is armed by quasi-connectivity (power through the block above it that it has not noticed); an update makes it push the package east, the redstone block lands beside the output, the moved observer fires and updates piston Q, which pushes the package home and re-arms P without an update. A plain piston interrupted mid-push leaves the same state as a normal retraction, so a quick second update strands nothing. Found by `mctas circuit bud census --base`.

The classic BUD: it sees blocks placed, removed or changed next to the target and pure block updates, which no observer can see: the smallest, 3 blocks. A sticky piston under a slime block and a redstone block is powered without having noticed it (the power reaches it only through the block above it, called quasi-connectivity); the first update makes it notice and lift the redstone block past the output for a moment, then pull it back, armed again. Detail: the landing slime block updates the piston through its head so it retracts, the redstone block landing last, so it re-arms without an update. A change by shape alone sends no block update: not detected; two updates 2 ticks apart jam it.

One observer facing the target: it sends a short pulse whenever that block is placed, broken, changed or grows. Copies can stand side by side, one per block. It does not see a block update that changes nothing, and a second change within 4 ticks is missed. Silent. Detail: the output is the observer's own 2-tick pulse, so neighbours' outputs never mix.

Tells when a block appears at the target or is taken away, and ignores the target's own changes (a crop growing, a door opening, a block turned): a fence beside the target and an observer watching it, 2 blocks. Copies can stack up a column, one per block. The fence bends toward any solid block placed at the target and straightens when it goes; the observer sends a short pulse each time. Detail: the fence's two other free sides sense too (footprint 3 cells); the output is the observer's own 2-tick pulse, and fences only connect sideways, so stacked copies never mix.

Tells when a block appears at the target or is taken away, sensing only that cell (nothing around it sets it off) and ignoring the target's own changes: 3 blocks. Copies can stand side by side, one per block. A torch under the target powers any solid block placed there, that block powers the dropper beside it, and the observer watching the dropper fires when the dropper's powered flag changes. Detail: the flag is set and cleared by that very update (a flags-2 change); turning the block in place keeps it powered, a change by shape alone or a pure update changes nothing: not detected. The output is the observer's own 2-tick pulse. The empty dropper clicks when it fires.

Tells when a block appears at the target or is taken away, sensing only that cell, silently: a torch, a lamp and an observer, 3 blocks. Copies can stand side by side, one per block. A torch under the target powers any solid block placed there, which lights the lamp beside it at once, and the observer watching the lamp fires. Detail: the lamp goes out 4 ticks after the block is removed, so a removal is seen 6 ticks late, and a block placed again within those 4 ticks finds the lamp still lit (re-arm 8 ticks); the output is the observer's own 2-tick pulse.

Turns on at the first block update next to the target and stays on until you reset it, reacting in 1 tick: the fastest latched BUD, 7 blocks. Copies can stand every 3 blocks. Detail: a sticky piston armed by quasi-connectivity (power that reaches it only through the block above its neighbor, so it has not noticed it) pushes a stone off the step between two dusts in the tick after the update; the low dust joins the powered high one and lights the output, and the piston stays out. The reset input is the arming redstone block: taking it away makes the piston pull the stone back (the output goes off 3 ticks later); putting it back arms it silently. The output is the low dust's own level.

The classic BUD, reacting in 1 tick: it also sees block updates that change nothing, which no observer can, 9 blocks. Copies can stand every 3 blocks. A stone stuck to the slime block cuts the step between two dusts; an update makes the piston push in the very next tick, the stone leaves the step and the low dust joins the powered high one, lighting the output until the stone comes back. Detail: the piston is armed by quasi-connectivity (power through the block above it that it has not noticed); a moving block conducts nothing, which is why the step opens at once. A change by shape alone sends no block update: not detected. The output is the low dust's own level.

Tells when a block is placed at the target, and ignores its removal and the target's own changes: 4 blocks. A redstone torch under the target powers any solid block placed there, which powers the sticky piston beside it; the piston lifts its observer, which fires once as it lands, into the output cell behind it (a 2-tick pulse). On removal the piston pulls the observer back down and it fires one cell lower, away from the output. Detail: turning the block in place, a shape-only change or a pure update leaves it powered: not detected.

Tells when a block is taken away from the target, and ignores its placement and the target's own changes: 4 blocks. A redstone torch under the target powers any solid block placed there, which powers the sticky piston beside it; the piston lifts its observer. When the block is removed the piston pulls the observer back down, and it fires once as it lands, into the output cell behind it (a 2-tick pulse); lifted, it fires one cell higher, away from the output. Detail: turning the block in place, a shape-only change or a pure update leaves the piston as it is: not detected.
